title: flatten collapses one level of a nested Result and keeps the inner failure in the combined error channel
notes: 01-result-lifting/result-tap-and-tap-error-observe-without-changing pins the observation members; this pins the one transformation member that was implemented and unreachable. `flatten` has existed on the runtime (poc/src/runtime/result.ts) with its own tests since before this case, and no `.sm` program could call it, because the member set an authored program may use is fixed by the checker prelude and the ownership walk's discharge set in poc/src/language/semantic.ts and neither had learned it. The refusal was not the obvious one: an undeclared member leaves the Result unconsumed, so the analyzer reported SMITHERS1301 and returned before the emitted TypeScript could report an unknown property — which is why a member can be implemented, tested, documented as required, and unreachable, without any gate going red. THE SECOND LINE IS THE POINT. `Result.try(() => lookup("zoe"))` is Ok(Err(Missing)), not Err: the body returns a Result rather than throwing, so the nesting is real and the inner failure is one level down. `no entry for zoe` proves flatten returned the INNER Result rather than the outer success, and the `Panic | Missing` error channel that reaches `.match` proves the two failure channels were combined rather than one of them dropped. `Result.try` over a Result-returning body is the authored form that builds the nesting at all; specification/failures.mdx §Authorability notes that `!` cannot produce it, since `!` marks its own output as a plain value. THE `xfail(go)` MARKER WAS RETIRED 2026-08-28, by making the fork's copy of the surface learn `flatten` rather than by softening the expectation: `compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt` now lists the member in `resultConsumerMembers` AND declares it on both `SmithersOk` and `SmithersErr`, which is what its own `len(resultConsumerDecls) != 2*len(resultConsumerMembers)` startup assertion demands. The fork's declaration is written over the whole `SmithersOk | SmithersErr` union through one shared `this` parameter, identical on both classes, because a union call intersects the constituents' `this` types and two different spellings would fail every call site with TS2684. The fork's copy can no longer drift from the reference's `RESULT_MEMBER_SIGNATURES` unnoticed: `compiler/fork_result_member_surface_test.go` reads both files and fails when the two name lists differ. The obligation this case discharges: specification/failures.mdx, "Matching and Transformation", lists the required transformation and sequencing members as `map mapError andThen andThenAsync flatten`, and that list is a direction obligation on an implementation.
